full_judgment:
8. Mr Afsar Hossain along with Mr Ahmed Sohel, the learned Advocates appearing for the respondents candidly submits that the petitioner has filed the writ petition after a lapse of 25 years for a declaration that the absorption of respondents is illegal. As such, simply on that score this Rule is liable to be discharged on the ground of inordinate delay. Further, he goes to submit that this Rule is not maintainable for the service matter so far respondents are concern is not amenable under writ jurisdiction. Moreover, the petitioner has tried to bring the service matter of the said respondents in the garb of public interest litigation though has failed miserably to how whose interest in fact he is espousing in the given facts and circumstances. Moreover, no where within the four corners of this writ petition it has been disclosed that the public at large are affected by the action of the respondent Nos. 1-4 appointing respondent Nos. 5-16 in their respective posts; and as such this writ petition cannot be treated as a public interest litigation. Me further submits that the petitioner has, in fact, filed the present writ petition with an ulterior motive in order to cause unnecessary harassment to the respondent Nos. 5-16 to serve the interest of vested quarters best known to him. Moreover, the paper clip-ping as annexed with the writ petition contained news item under the leading "317 fake government employees are found" published in the Daily "Prothom Alo" dated 8-9-2008 whereas he filed the writ petition only against 12 persons i.e., the respondent Nos. 5-16, which goes to disclose malafide act and a such on that score as well this Rule must fail. He also submits that the Gazetted Officers (Department of National Savings, Ministry of Finance) Recruitment Rules, 1979 is not applicable to these respondents, for they were not appointed directly as fresh candidates. The petitioner rather made an abortive effort to confuse this Hon'ble Court placing the said Rules, 1979 for appointment of the respondents instead of the Ordinance, 1985 hence; this Rule suffers from suppression of fact. Moreover, he submits that respondent Nos. 5, 7, 14 and 15 have already been retired from their service and that the rest are on the verge of retirement within one year. Because of the pendency of his Rule filed without any legal basis whatsoever The said retired respondents arc now living in distress and hardship and that they are not receiving any pension benefit due to the pendency of the Rule in spite of serving in their respective posts for 27 (twenty seven) years hence those respondents are seriously prejudiced. Accordingly, he submits that the petitioner having failed to substantiate any of the grounds which he has agitated this Rule should be discharged with costs. 

 "It is now well-settled that a statement of fact contained in a newspaper is merely evidence in the absence of the maker of the statement appearing in Court and deposing to have perceived the fact reported 

 "A newspaper report without any further proof of what had actually happened through witnesses is of no value. It is at best a second hand secondary evidence. It is well known that reporters collect information and pass it on to the editor who edits the news item and then publishes it. In this process the truth might get perverted or garbled. Such news items cannot be said to prove themselves although they may be taken into account with other evidence if the other evidence is forcible.
